title: 1994 AHSME Problem 3
statement: How many of the following are equal to \(x^x+x^x\) for all \(x\gt0?\) \[ \begin{aligned} \mathrm{I:}\quad&2x^x\\ \mathrm{II:}\quad&x^{2x}\\ \mathrm{III:}\quad&(2x)^x\\ \mathrm{IV:}\quad&(2x)^{2x} \end{aligned} \]

solutions.text: The given sum is \(2x^x,\) so expression I is always equal to it. Expression II fails at \(x=1,\) where its value is \(1\) instead of \(2.\) Expression III fails at \(x=2,\) where its value is \(16\) instead of \(8.\) Expression IV fails at \(x=1,\) where its value is \(4\) instead of \(2.\) Hence only one expression works. Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: First combine the two identical terms
Test whether changing the base or exponent preserves \(2x^x\) for every \(x\)
